questions.exp: Erythropoiesis: hematopoietic stem cell → BFU-E (burst forming unit-erythroid) → CFU (colony forming unit) → erythroblast → reticulocyte → erythrocyte (RBC). (Book p808)

questions.q: Reticulocyte to erythrocyte (RBC) takes:

units.title: Consequences of CKD: the acidosis branch
units.guide: CKD consequences: access dialysis, acidosis, anemia. Acidosis: NAGMA → HAGMA, myocardial depressant; monitor venous HCO₃⁻ (normal 20-22 mEq/L); Rx oral/IV sodium bicarbonate. Anemia appears below GFR 75 ml/min (male) / 40 ml/min (female).

units.title: Anemia thresholds: ISN, KDIGO and the ESA target
units.guide: Start evaluation: ISN <11 gm/dl; KDIGO male <13 g/dl, female <12 g/dl. Target Hb on exogenous erythropoietin (ESA): 11.5-12.5 g/dl; >13 gm/dl → stroke, thrombosis.

units.title: Erythropoiesis: stages, dependencies and timing
units.guide: Hematopoietic stem cell → BFU-E → CFU → erythroblast → reticulocyte → RBC. EPO-independent (stem cell → BFU-E); erythropoietin-dependent (BFU-E → CFU → erythroblast, 10-14 days); iron + erythropoietin dependent (erythroblast → reticulocyte 4 days → RBC 1-2 days).

units.title: Causes: EPO, iron, inflammation, PTH and deficiencies
units.guide: Normocytic normochromic anemia: ↓ RBC production (more common) >> ↑ RBC destruction (↓ survival span). ↓EPO inappropriately low for anemia/hypoxia via the HIF-α/HIF-PH axis (normal O₂ degrades HIF-α; hypoxia → HIF-α+HIF-β → EPO from peritubular interstitial fibroblasts, cortex > outer medulla). Low iron: anorexia, ↓ absorption, blood loss (1 ml = 0.5 mg Fe). Inflammation → activin/CRP/interleukin → ↑ hepcidin → ↓ EPO response. Raised PTH → marrow fibrosis. Deficiency: vitamin B₆, folic acid. Note: uremic toxins inhibit erythropoiesis; RBC glutathione depletion shortens survival — EPO effect ↑↑ after dialysis.

units.title: Effects of anemia and STEP 1 iron replenishment
units.guide: Anemia independently raises the risk of fall in GFR; LVH; cardiovascular mortality (m/c cause of death) via LVH, calcification, endothelial dysfunction. STEP 1: replenish iron store = 2.2 × BW × (Hb deficit) + 1000 mg (as printed; the common Ganzoni 2.4 is not the page's value).

units.title: Iron therapy: oral and IV, ferritin and TSAT
units.guide: Oral: ferrous sulfate 60 mg elemental iron — non-dialysable patients, less effective. IV: ferric carboxymaltose 1 gm in 100 ml NS over 10-15 min; iron sucrose 200 mg; iron isomaltose 1 gm. Note: low s. ferritin → anemia; normal → check TSAT = s. iron/TIBC × 100; s. iron ↓ = TSAT ↓ (TSAT: transferrin saturation; TIBC: total iron binding capacity).

units.title: ESA: prerequisites, contraindications, generations and dosing
units.guide: STEP 2 ESA. Prerequisites (enough iron store): TSAT ≥30%, s. ferritin ≥500 ng/ml. C/I: absolute — stroke; relative — malignancy. SC preferred (30% less dose); IV. 1st gen EPO-α: T½ 8.5 hrs, 50-100 U/kg/week or 4000-10000 U/week, up to 300 U/kg/week. No response = ESA hyporesponsiveness (m/c: iron deficiency; chronic disease). Daprodustat: prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, oral, high cost. 2nd gen (2 extra N-linked glycosylation chains): darbepoetin α T½ 25.3 hrs, 60-200 µg/2 weekly; EPO-β (CERA) T½ 130 hrs, 0.6 µg/kg/2 weekly.
